pi-01.exam.tasks.0.desc:
You are given a dictionary of player levels. Find the player with the highest level and print: Чемпион: имя (уровень N)

Expected output: Чемпион: sara (уровень 12)
pi-01.exam.tasks.0.title: Player database
pi-01.lessons.0.blocks.0.html: A dictionary (dict) stores key: value pairs in curly braces. It works like a real dictionary: you look up a word (the key) and find its translation (the value):
pi-01.lessons.0.blocks.2.html: In a list you fetch elements by position, in a dictionary by key. That is far handier when the data has meaningful names.
pi-01.lessons.0.title: A dictionary is data with names
pi-01.lessons.1.blocks.0.html: To add or change a value, simply assign by key:
pi-01.lessons.1.blocks.2.html: Check whether a key exists with the in operator:
pi-01.lessons.1.title: Modifying a dictionary
pi-01.lessons.2.blocks.0.html: If the key is missing, player['xp'] crashes the program with a KeyError. The get() method returns None or a default instead of raising:
pi-01.lessons.2.blocks.2.html: The classic way to count things: counts[x] = counts.get(x, 0) + 1
pi-01.lessons.2.title: get() — safe access
pi-01.lessons.3.blocks.0.html: You can loop over a dictionary. Three ways:
pi-01.lessons.3.blocks.2.html: .keys() — all the keys, .values() — all the values, .items() — the pairs. Most of the time you want .items().
pi-01.lessons.3.title: Looping over a dictionary
pi-01.lessons.4.blocks.0.html: A dictionary value can be anything — even a list or another dictionary. That is how complex data is built:
pi-01.lessons.4.blocks.2.html: Read the chain left to right: take team['aziz'] (a dictionary) → from it ['items'] (a list) → from it [0] (an element). This is exactly what data from real APIs and databases looks like!
pi-01.lessons.4.title: Nested structures
pi-01.quiz.2.explain: Square brackets with a missing key raise KeyError. The safe way is get().
pi-01.quiz.2.q: What happens if you access a missing key with [ ]?
pi-01.quiz.3.explain: The second argument of get() is the default used when the key is missing.
pi-01.quiz.3.q: What does d.get('x', 99) return when the key x is absent?
pi-01.quiz.4.explain: Just assign to a new key: d['xp'] = 100.
pi-01.quiz.4.q: How do you add the key “xp” with value 100 to the dictionary d?
pi-01.quiz.5.explain: .items() returns pairs — convenient in a loop: for k, v in d.items():
pi-01.quiz.5.q: What does the .items() method give you?
pi-01.quiz.6.explain: First the key “a” gives the list [10, 20], then element [1] of it — that is 20.
pi-01.tagline: Key-value pairs and how to work with them
pi-01.tasks.0.desc: Create a dictionary hero with the keys name = "Рыцарь" and hp = 100. Then add the key gold with value 50 and reduce hp by 30. Print the dictionary.
pi-01.tasks.0.title: Hero profile
pi-01.tasks.1.desc:
You are given a dictionary of prices. Print every item as товар - цена монет and the total at the end as Всего: сумма:

зелье - 30 монет
эликсир - 80 монет
яд - 45 монет
Всего: 155
pi-01.tasks.1.hint: for name, price in shop.items(): print(f'{name} - {price} монет'), then print(f'Всего: {sum(shop.values())}')
pi-01.tasks.1.title: Potion shop
pi-01.tasks.2.desc: You are given a list of votes for players. Count the votes into a dictionary votes and print it. Expected result: {'aziz': 3, 'timur': 2, 'bek': 1}
pi-01.tasks.2.hint: for name in voting: votes[name] = votes.get(name, 0) + 1 — get returns 0 for a new name.
pi-01.tasks.2.title: Vote counter
pi-01.title: Dictionaries
pi-02.exam.questions.2.q: How do you stop a loop from the inside?
pi-02.exam.questions.4.q: Which loop suits “ask for the password until it is correct”?
pi-02.exam.tasks.0.desc:
A deposit holds 1000 sum and grows by 10% every year (money *= 1.1). Use while to count how many years it takes to exceed 2000 and print: Лет: N

Expected output: Лет: 8
pi-02.exam.tasks.0.title: Bank deposit
pi-02.lessons.0.blocks.0.html: for repeats a known number of times, while while repeats as long as a condition is true. How many times is unknown in advance:
pi-02.lessons.0.blocks.2.html: The shape: check the condition → run the body → check again → … As soon as the condition becomes False, the loop ends.
pi-02.lessons.0.title: while — the «until» loop
pi-02.lessons.1.blocks.0.html: If the condition NEVER becomes false, the program hangs forever:
pi-02.lessons.1.blocks.2.html: The rule: something inside while must change the variable in the condition. Check yourself by asking: “when will this loop end?”
pi-02.lessons.1.title: Infinite loops — the main hazard
pi-02.lessons.2.blocks.0.html: A popular technique: loop forever and leave with break when the awaited event happens:
pi-02.lessons.2.blocks.2.html: Game loops, menus and command handling are written this way: “keep working until the user says quit”.
pi-02.lessons.2.title: while True + break
pi-02.lessons.3.blocks.0.html: A while classic: keep asking until the user types a valid value:
pi-02.lessons.3.title: Validating user input
pi-02.lessons.4.blocks.0.html:
• for — when you know HOW MANY times or WHAT you iterate over: a list, a range, a string
  • while — when you repeat UNTIL AN EVENT: while alive, until guessed, until “stop” is typed
pi-02.lessons.4.title: for vs while — which to choose
pi-02.quiz.0.explain: while runs WHILE the condition is True and stops once it turns False.
pi-02.quiz.0.q: When does a while loop end?
pi-02.quiz.1.explain: x is always 0, the condition is forever True — the program hangs. The body needs x += 1.
pi-02.quiz.1.options.1: x never changes — the loop is infinite
pi-02.quiz.1.options.2: while cannot be used with print
pi-02.quiz.1.q: What is wrong with this code?
pi-02.quiz.2.explain: n counts down: 3, 2, 1. At n = 0 the condition is false — stop.
pi-02.quiz.3.explain: while True runs forever and you leave through break, driven by an event.
pi-02.quiz.3.options.1: A loop until break — leaving on an event
pi-02.quiz.3.q: What is the while True technique for?
pi-02.quiz.4.explain: The condition 10 < 5 is false IMMEDIATELY — the body never runs.
pi-02.quiz.4.q: How many times does the body run?
pi-02.quiz.5.explain: while is for when the number of repetitions is unknown up front: “until guessed”, “until stop is typed”.
pi-02.quiz.5.q: When is while better than for?
pi-02.tasks.0.desc: Print every power of two below 100, each on its own line: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64.
pi-02.tasks.0.hint: while n < 100: print(n) and n *= 2 (multiply n by 2).
pi-02.tasks.0.title: Powers of two
pi-02.tasks.1.desc: A rocket is at 1000 m and descends 150 m every second. Print the altitude each second (Высота: X) while it is above 0, then print the line Посадка!
pi-02.tasks.1.hint: while height > 0: print(f"Высота: {height}") and height -= 150. print("Посадка!") goes after the loop, unindented.
pi-02.tasks.1.title: Rocket landing
pi-02.tasks.2.desc:
The secret number is 7. In a loop the program reads guesses through input(): if the guess is lower it prints Больше!, if higher — Меньше!, and on a correct guess — Победа! and leaves the loop.

The check will enter: 3, 9, 7.
pi-02.tasks.2.hint: if guess < secret: print("Больше!") elif guess > secret: print("Меньше!") else: print("Победа!") and break
pi-02.tasks.2.title: Guess the number
pi-02.title: while loops
pi-03.exam.questions.5.q: How many parameters of def f(a, b, c=1): may be omitted?
pi-03.exam.tasks.0.desc: Write a function grade(score): 90+ → "A", 70–89 → "B", 50–69 → "C", below 50 → "F". Print grade(95), grade(71) and grade(30), each on its own line.
pi-03.exam.tasks.0.title: Grade from score
pi-03.lessons.0.blocks.0.html: A function is a named piece of code you can call as many times as you like. You already use other people's: print(), len(), input(). Time to write your own!
pi-03.lessons.0.blocks.2.html: def name(): is the declaration, the body is indented. Important: the function's code runs only when it is called as name(), not when it is declared.
pi-03.lessons.0.title: A function is your own building block
pi-03.lessons.1.blocks.0.html: The brackets declare parameters — the data the function accepts:
pi-03.lessons.1.blocks.2.html: Parameters can have default values — then you may leave them out:
pi-03.lessons.1.title: Parameters — a function's input
pi-03.lessons.2.blocks.0.html: return sends a result back out — you can store it in a variable and use it further:
pi-03.lessons.2.blocks.2.html: ⚠️ The difference EVERY beginner confuses: print merely shows something on screen, while return hands a value back to the program. After return the function ends immediately:
pi-03.lessons.2.title: return — a function's output
pi-03.lessons.3.blocks.0.html: Variables created inside a function are local: they are invisible from outside:
pi-03.lessons.3.blocks.2.html: A good habit: a function takes everything through parameters and gives everything back through return. Such code is easy to read and to test.
pi-03.lessons.3.title: Variable scope
pi-03.lessons.4.blocks.0.html: A large program is a set of small functions, each doing one thing:
pi-03.lessons.4.blocks.2.html: A function can call another function — that is how a house is built from bricks. This is a programmer's core skill!
pi-03.lessons.4.title: Building a program out of functions
pi-03.quiz.1.explain: The function was called twice — the body ran twice.
pi-03.quiz.2.explain: return gives a value back so the code can use it; print only writes to the screen.
pi-03.quiz.2.options.1: print shows on screen, return hands the value to the program
pi-03.quiz.2.q: What is the difference between print and return?
pi-03.quiz.3.explain: double(3) = 6, double(6) = 12. Function calls can be nested.
pi-03.quiz.4.q: What does a function without return give back?
pi-03.quiz.5.explain: No argument was passed — the default value “гость” is used.
pi-03.quiz.6.explain: After return the function ends at once — print('после') is unreachable.
pi-03.tasks.0.desc:
Write a function welcome(name, level) that returns (return!) the string name [уровень level] вошёл в игру.

For example, welcome("Азиз", 5) → Азиз [уровень 5] вошёл в игру
pi-03.tasks.0.hint: return f'{name} [уровень {level}] вошёл в игру' — and remove the pass.
pi-03.tasks.0.title: Level greeting
pi-03.tasks.1.desc: Write a function max3(a, b, c) that returns the largest of three numbers. The built-in max() is not allowed — use if only!
pi-03.tasks.1.hint: if a >= b and a >= c: return a — and likewise for each. Or compare one by one against a best variable.
pi-03.tasks.1.title: Maximum of three
pi-03.tasks.2.desc:
Write two functions:

  • xp_for_level(level) — returns level * 100
  • total_xp(levels) — takes a list of levels and returns the total XP for all of them, using the first function

total_xp([1, 2, 3]) → 600
pi-03.tasks.2.hint: total = 0, then for lvl in levels: total += xp_for_level(lvl), and return total at the end.
pi-03.tasks.2.title: XP calculator
pi-03.title: Functions
